title: Which expression gives the money earned from two kinds of plates?
description: A seller earns thirty rupees from each plate of Jowar roti and twenty rupees from each plate of pulao. The amount from each kind is written with a letter for the plates, and the two amounts are added and checked.
teaching_notes: One idea: the money from one kind of plate is its price times the number of plates, and the totals of the two kinds are added. Watch for students who add the two prices first and then multiply by the plates of both kinds.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of counting each kind and adding the counts: the money from each kind of plate is written, and the two amounts are added.
video_script.substitution: The method of counting horizontal and diagonal matchsticks separately and adding, with the money from each kind of plate in place of the matchsticks.
video_script.anchor: a stall with plates of Jowar roti at thirty rupees and plates of pulao at twenty rupees
video_script.payoff_line: The total earned is thirty x plus twenty y rupees

final_answer.spoken: thirty x plus twenty y rupees

never_show: the finished expression before the answer beat
maths_rules: Jowar roti: 30 rupees x x plates = 30x
other expressions at x = 2, y = 1: swapped prices 70, (30 + 20) x (x + y) 150, subtraction 40
video_script.design: One idea: money from one kind is price times plates, and the two kinds are added. Assumes the example of counting each kind and adding. The stall with two kinds of plates stays on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>A plate of Jowar roti costs thirty rupees, and a plate of pulao costs twenty rupees.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>In one day, x plates of Jowar roti and y plates of pulao were ordered.
<bookmark mark='p4'/>Which expression describes the total amount earned that day?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: money from one kind of plate = price of one plate times the number of plates ; the letters x and y stand for the plates

marks.g2: the price times the number of plates is written under the row

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Each plate of one kind brings the same amount of money.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>The money from one kind is the price of one plate times the number of plates.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>The letters x and y stand for how many plates were ordered.

beats.on_screen: Given: Jowar roti costs 30 rupees a plate ; pulao costs 20 rupees a plate ; x plates of Jowar roti and y plates of pulao

marks.gv2: x plates and y plates are written

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, Jowar roti costs thirty rupees a plate, and pulao costs twenty rupees a plate.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>The plates ordered are x of Jowar roti and y of pulao.

beats.on_screen: To find: the expression for the total amount earned in rupees
narration: <bookmark mark='fd'/>We find the total amount in rupees. We work the same way as the example in your book. Take each kind on its own, and then add.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: Jowar roti: 30 rupees × x plates = 30x rupees

marks.s1a: 30 × x is written for the Jowar roti

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>First, the Jowar roti. Each of the x plates brings thirty rupees, so it brings thirty times x rupees.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: pulao: 20 rupees × y plates = 20y rupees

marks.s2a: 20 × y is written for the pulao

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Second, the pulao. Each of the y plates brings twenty rupees, so it brings twenty times y rupees.

marks.s3a: the two amounts are joined with a plus sign

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Third, the two amounts are added to give the total. The prices stay with their own plates and are never added first.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check with x = 2 and y = 1: 30 × 2 + 20 × 1 = 60 + 20 = 80 ; the other expressions give 70, 150, 101 and 40

marks.s4a: 2 and 1 replace x and y in the total
marks.s4b: the other expressions are tried with 2 and 1 and do not give 80

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Fourth, check with two plates of Jowar roti and one plate of pulao. That is sixty rupees and twenty rupees, which is eighty rupees.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Our total gives thirty times two plus twenty times one, which is also eighty. The other expressions do not give eighty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The total earned is thirty x plus twenty y rupees.
